candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Marcellinum de Interpretatione Psalmorum (Letter to Marcellinus on the Interpretation of the Psalms), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 27 (1857). The Letter is Athanasius's principal pastoral-spiritual work — a personal letter to Marcellinus (recovering from illness) explaining how to use each Psalm as prayer for specific spiritual circumstances. Hermeneutic anchor for the Tewahedo Office (Säʿatat) Psalter-recitation tradition.
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Marcellinum §16 (c. 350 AD)

'O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee' (LXX 87:2) — Athanasius marks Ps 88 (LXX 87) as the AFFLICTION-PRAYER PARADIGM in the Letter to Marcellinus: prescribed for the soul-in-affliction-without-relief. Ps 88 is the darkest of the canonical Psalms (ending on darkness, not deliverance — phrasē mou aphēste philos kai plēsion kai tous gnōstous mou apo talaipōrias, 'thou hast put far from me lover and friend, and my acquaintances into darkness'). Athanasius's pastoral-counsel: the Psalter does not prescribe Ps 88 lightly; but for the soul-in-severe-affliction, even the dark-Psalm is Spirit-given consolation — the very-act-of-voicing-affliction-to-God IS the saving-prayer.
